question.text: Compound (A), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>9</mn></msub><mi>Cl</mi></math>, gives a white precipitate when warmed with alcoholic <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>AgNO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math><sub>.</sub> Oxidation of (A) gives an acid (B), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math>. (B) easily forms anhydride on heating. Identify the compound (A).

solution.text: Compound (A) gives a white precipitate when warmed with alcoholic AgNO3means it contain a removable chloride atom(Benzylic position). Oxidation of (A) gives an acid (B), C8H6O4. (B) easily forms anhydride on heating. Means both acid should be ortho position of each other.
